extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for AMS proceedings and collections using AMS-LATEX
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing source files (LaTeX + graphics + bibliographies) for submission to AMS proceedings and collections, using the AMS-LaTeX document classes and meeting AMS production requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the supplied template/class
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for your particular publication and the appropriate document class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy the template to a suitably named file and use the specific AMS document class (e.g., \documentclass{pspum-l}). The templates include starter theorem sets and recommended packages. Do not change to a non-AMS class if submitting to AMS proceedings/collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should not exceed 20 characters and consist only of numeric or unaccented ASCII alphabetic characters. Avoid overly generic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid names like article.tex, mybib.tex, fig1.eps. Use identifiable short names to reduce chance of name conflicts. Bundle multiple files in a zip for submission to avoid transmission or naming problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or layout dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions; page sizes must conform to the publication's specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text width is determined by the trim size; changing widths or dimensions will alter line breaks (critical for math displays, tables, and figures) and will be reverted by production, possibly introducing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change default font size for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify the default font size except temporarily for proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using 11pt/12pt affects line breaks and display layout; if used for proofreading, reprocess and check breaks before submission and then revert for final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN packages (and avoid unsupported packages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 'public' packages available from CTAN; do not load unsupported or problematic packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended/compatible: amssymb, graphicx, longtable, mathrsfs, mathtools, natbib (with caveats), upref, tikz, xypic. Packages to avoid: biblatex (not supported), epsfig (superseded), diagrams (contains a 'time bomb'), geometry (changes page dimensions), microtype (not supported), parskip (redefines ToC processing). Don't load packages you don't need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Built-in AMS packages: amsthm, amsmath, amsfonts handling
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS classes incorporate amsthm and automatically load amsmath; amsfonts is loaded unless [noamsfonts] is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not explicitly request these in most cases. Consult the respective user guides (amsthm, amsmath, AMSFonts) for usage details. Rely on AMS theorem facilities and amsmath structures for displays and theorem environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine core LaTeX/AMS commands; use \newcommand
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeﬁne any existing LaTeX or AMS-LATEX commands. Use \newcommand, not \def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \newcommand warns if the name is already used. Redefinitions can break AMS production. Remove unused command definitions before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place macro definitions in the preamble and use consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Put definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions together in the preamble and use the macro for every occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use author-defined macros in author names, titles, abstracts, section and theorem headings, or references. Use macros for repeated mathematical expressions only; remove unused macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in titles and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of math in the title and in other headings because titles are used by online bibliographic services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEX math coding (especially $...$) in titles can produce inaccurate bibliographic listings and problematic PDF bookmarks. If math is necessary, use only fonts compatible with AMS production (Computer Modern, amsfonts/amssymb, mathrsfs script).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) using \subjclass[2010]
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers representing primary and secondary subjects and enter them with \subjclass[2010].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one primary classification is required; use full numbers and consult www.ams.org/msc. Omitting [2010] defaults to 1991 scheme; upgrade AMS classes if 2010 is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics must conform to AMS graphics guidelines and fit margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure graphics do not extend into margins and conform to AMS graphics guidelines (file format, resolution, color, fonts, sizing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 for file formats, resolution (photographs >=300 dpi at final size), color space (CMYK preferred for print), font sizes in graphics, and cropping/bounding box requirements. Check figures printed in black and white if they might be printed grayscale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use TeX coding to force line/page breaks or explicit spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use TeX coding to control line and page breaks or explicit horizontal/vertical spacing commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production may change line and page breaks; manual breaks will have to be removed and may introduce errors or require extra work. Avoid \vspace, \hspace, manual breaks, and \parskip adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering style and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS style requires equation numbers to be on the left, flush with the left margin (default [leqno]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiline equation numbering defaults to vertically centered (option [centertags]); [tbtags] can place numbers on first/last line. Right-side numbering ([reqno]) is supported but strongly discouraged as incompatible with \qed boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \cite for citations (and avoid \cite in abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cite to indicate citations in the manuscript; \cite may not appear in an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal references should use \label and \ref (or \eqref for equations). For author-year styles natbib or amsrefs features are available; do not invent citation formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include complete bibliographic information and use ABMR abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all available information for references and use the abbreviations for journals and book series from ABMR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic data will be replaced in production by amsrefs form from MathSciNet (enhanced references). If using BibTeX, insert the contents of the .bbl into the .tex file; do not send .bib. Use amsplain.bst or amsalpha.bst if using BibTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-matter tags: required and optional fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate top-matter tags: required include \title, \author, \address, \subjclass[2010], \begin{abstract}...\end{abstract}, and \maketitle; others (\contrib, \curraddr, \email, \urladdr, \dedicatory, \thanks, \keywords) are optional as indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place top-matter after \begin{document}. Provide short forms in bracketed arguments when needed for running heads. Do not use macros in top-matter fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and running head formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page must contain a descriptive title; capitalize only the first word, first word after ':' and proper nouns. Supply a shortened title for running heads if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague phrases like 'some remarks about'. For very long author lists provide shortened running-head forms. Do not use author-defined macros in titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract placement and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the abstract before \maketitle; it may have multiple paragraphs and displayed material; suggested upper limits ~150 words (short articles) and ~300 words (long articles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use author-defined macros, \cite, or \ref in the abstract. If abstract is after \maketitle a warning will be generated and it will be printed in place incorrectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble: documentclass options and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate \documentclass options: default paper size [letterpaper] (use [a4paper] for drafts outside U.S.), [twoside] default (use [oneside] for drafts), version [draft]/[final], default font size [10pt], equation numbering options ([leqno] default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid [reqno] (right numbering) for production reasons. Use [fleqn] if flush-left displays are desired; be aware of indentation \mathindent. Use [draft] to mark overfull boxes during proofreading, but submit [final].

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended and problem-causing packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Some packages are recommended (amssymb, graphicx, longtable, mathrsfs, mathtools, natbib, upref, tikz, xypic); others cause problems and should be avoided (biblatex, epsfig, diagrams, geometry, microtype, parskip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not load packages that aren't needed. If a package appears to work locally, it may still break AMS production style or automation; check the Author Handbook lists and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: New command declarations placement and hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Place all new-command definitions in the preamble; use \newcommand and remove commands that haven't been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not redefine LaTeX, amsmath, or AMS class commands. Use AMS-provided environments (e.g., proof) rather than defining replacements. Avoid macros for ordinary text to preserve indexing and online indexing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem declarations and styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare theorem types in the preamble using \theoremstyle and \newtheorem. Three predefined styles: plain (italic text), definition (upright text), remark (upright text, no extra space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number theorems consecutively or within sections via \newtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section]; number different theorem types consecutively with [thm] as needed. Use amsthm facilities rather than the obsolete LATEX theorem package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and labels for cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use up to five heading levels (\part, \specialsection, \section, \subsection, \subsubsection). Any heading may be given a \label directly after the heading for references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references require at least two LaTeX runs for proper resolution. Heed 'Cross references may have changed...' warnings. Use \ref for sections and \eqref for equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical text coding and roman type usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expressions should be coded as math ($...$ or \(...\)); numbers, punctuation, parentheses, bracket labels, and symbols used as labels should be set in roman (upright) type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mathematical elements from textual ones; use \textup{...} in non-roman environments, standard control sequences for functions (log, lim), and \DeclareMathOperator for new operator names. Use upref package to force roman cross-references when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed equations: breaks, alignment, and width
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully for proper breaking, alignment, and that they do not exceed page width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiline displays use amsmath structures. Ensure displays fit within the publication's text width to avoid production adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises: use xca environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the xca environment for producing exercises that appear individually within a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare xca in preamble with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem; it behaves like other theorem-class environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: request AMS assistance if including an index
rubrics_metrics.description: If an index is required in a proceedings volume, the editor should request instructions and assistance from AMS technical support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing in proceedings is unusual and may require special production steps; contact AMS technical support for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floats: numbering, placement, referencing, and section-locality
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats (figures/tables) should be numbered consistently, placed at top or bottom of page, have an in-text reference, and appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place a figure/table before its first reference unless both appear on the same page spread. Allow floats to float (avoid [h!] option) to prevent pagination problems during production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions: placement and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are usually below figures and above tables. A reference label should usually be associated with the caption and must be given after the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the AMS caption style (caption packages may change style and should be avoided). Provide descriptive caption text or omit if none is needed. Use \label after \caption and refer to the float with \ref{...}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering floats: unnecessary with AMS classes
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS classes center content of table and figure environments automatically; explicit \centering or center environments are unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add additional centering commands; the classes handle centering and caption styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics file formats and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide graphics in appropriate file formats and resolution: photos minimum 300 dpi at final printed size; acceptable file formats include EPS, TIFF, JPEG (for photos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX. Vector graphics (TikZ, PSTricks) should be included as code or as separate input files if large. Check bounding boxes and cropping; name files per naming convention. AMS will analyze and optimize color graphics for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics: CMYK requirement for print and RGB conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics intended to be printed in color should be submitted in CMYK format; RGB files will be converted to CMYK by AMS and color reproduction cannot be guaranteed to match the RGB file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color graphics will be printed in black & white or grayscale, convert them to grayscale before submission and check legibility on a black-and-white printer, since light colors may disappear when converted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colored lines and shades guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Colored lines must be no less than 0.5 point in width; inherently light colors (yellow, cyan) should be near 100% tint and handled carefully as 50% tints may become invisible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on subtle tints for critical information. Check conversion to grayscale for legibility and ensure lines are thick enough to reproduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type in graphics: minimum size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Type within graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%; do not put type on a dark background, and check that grayscale reproduction is legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small type that looks fine on-screen may be unreadable in print or at lower screen resolutions (72 PPI). Use consistent fonts for labels (packages that apply labels help consistency) but ensure labels lie within graphic boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: width, rotation, and caption placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure table width does not exceed the text block. Very wide tables may be rotated using rotating package and sidewaystable; set captions above the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate tables so the left-hand side becomes the page bottom after rotation. For detailed table formatting consult The LaTeX Companion or referenced resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using label-applying packages: watch for label overflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that apply labels to graphics keep fonts consistent but labels do not change graphic dimensions and may extend beyond the graphic into margins or overprint surrounding material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check for labels extending outside graphic boundaries and add extra space (e.g., with \vspace) if necessary to avoid overprinting or margin intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX-native graphics: recommended environments
rubrics_metrics.description: For TeX-generated graphics, recommended environments include tikz/PGF, pstricks, and xypic; these are suitable for diagrams and other drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikZ/PGF works with dvips and pdfLaTeX and has extensive documentation. PSTricks is powerful but more dvips-centric. See manuals and primers referenced in the handbook for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission: send only required files and ensure exact match to accepted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, send only the source files needed to produce the accepted copy, and ensure they exactly match the accepted reference copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude .log and .aux files. If multiple files, bundle with zip. Preferred submission is via web server (requires AMS web account); email submissions go to pub-submit@ams.org with attachments and subject line including publication code and editor names. Production begins once signed consent/copyright is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish / Copyright handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent when the accepted work is received; production begins once a signed form is received. Authors retain rights to reuse their own work but may be asked to transfer other rights to AMS; public domain dedication possible after 28 years if copyright transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return the form promptly. Understand rights retained and any optional transfers; contact AMS for specific rights questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography preparation: amsrefs or BibTeX (no biblatex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies may be prepared using amsrefs or BibTeX; biblatex and other methods are not supported by AMS production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using BibTeX, use amsplain.bst or amsalpha.bst and insert the .bbl contents into the .tex file for submission. Expect AMS to replace or enhance references using MathSciNet data (enhanced references), which may add DOIs and links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced references from MathSciNet
rubrics_metrics.description: References will be replaced or enhanced by AMS with data from MathSciNet in amsrefs format, adding DOIs, links, and standardized bibliographic information when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every reference has a MathSciNet record; enhancement may cause style inconsistencies or reveal incorrect MR numbers. Report errors to eprod-support@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to get help and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should consult AMS Author FAQ, AMS technical support, CTAN, TUG, and online forums (comp.text.tex, tex.stackexchange.com) for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS technical support contacts and acquisitions/webmaster emails and phone numbers are provided. Use online documentation (amsmath, amsthm, tikz manuals) and community resources for platform-specific or LaTeX questions.
